gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's 350W panel has a 33 V open-circuit voltage, so two of them in series reach 66 V, over the 60 V solar-input limit on both the Elite 200 V2 and the AC180. The Elite 200 V2 + 2×350W bundle therefore has to be wired in parallel, and neither the bundle's box list nor the panel's box list includes the MC4 Y-branch connectors that parallel wiring needs.
standout_why: I compared against ecosolarkits.com (cited), wattfolk.com (cited) and cleanpowerguide.com. Ecosolarkits says only that you should confirm your power station's input voltage and watt limits, and it gives no panel voltages. Wattfolk says 'Wire in series for 24V or in parallel for 12V' for an ECO-WORTHY kit and generally tells you to 'confirm your power station's input voltage and watt limits'. Cleanpowerguide says to size from cold-weather open-circuit voltage but names no product. None of them names a bundle whose own two panels break the station's 60 V limit in series, or the connector that is missing. The obvious trap, LiFePO4 not charging below 32°F, is already on ecosolarkits ('should not be charged below about 32°F unless they have self-heating') and on wattfolk, so it doesn't stand out. I could not read agripure.org (cited) or solargenadvisor.com (rank 1) because both failed with a self-signed certificate error.
kit_items: power station: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2. Its solar input takes 12–60 V at up to 20 A and 1,000 W, which is twice the AC180's 10 A, so a high-current panel isn't clipped as hard.

solar panel: one BLUETTI 350W Solar Panel. At 33 V open-circuit it sits inside the 12–60 V window as a single panel, and it ships with its own 20A MC4-to-XT60 cable, so you need no extra adapter or wiring choice.
avoid: Elite 200 V2 + 2×350W ($2,148) unless you add MC4 Y-branch connectors and wire the panels in parallel. In series they reach 66 V. In parallel the station still caps input at 20 A.
avoid for a 350W pair: AC180. Its input is capped at 12–60 V and 10 A, so two 350W panels go over the limit in series and are clipped to 10 A in parallel.

findings.label: Series voltage of the bundle's two panels vs the station's limit
findings.value: 66 V in series vs 60 V max input
findings.note: Arithmetic: 2 × 33 V = 66 V, which is 6 V over the 60 V limit on the Elite 200 V2 page. This is at standard test conditions. Open-circuit voltage rises in cold weather, so the margin only gets worse in winter. The panels must go in parallel, where the station caps input current at 20 A.

findings.note: StorageReview lists no separate charging-temperature range. The listed storage minimum of 32 °F matters for a unit left in an unheated shed over winter.

findings.label: Cold-weather charging behavior
findings.value: Charging stops below 32 °F (0 °C). 100 W heating pads switch on below 32 °F and off at 41 °F (5 °C), then charging resumes. Discharge stops below −4 °F.
findings.note: Text read from the Redodo store's product search data with storecheck. A direct WebFetch of the page returned HTTP 429. Price $251.99 on 2026-11-10. This is relevant to a DIY 12 V shed build, but rivals already cover the general freezing-charge rule.
